newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris Bourse volume up 60 percent in first half.
newsitem.headline: Paris Bourse volume up 60 percent in first half.

text.p: The Paris stock exchange recorded its highest ever half yearly volume in the first six months of 1997, Bourse head Jean-Francois Theodore said on Thursday.
Some 1,119.13 billion francs worth of French shares traded during the period, a 60.6 percent increase from the first half of 1996.
Theodore also said the bourse was studying whether to extend trading hours as a large proportion of transactions take place between 1300 GMT and 1500 GMT, once Wall Street is open.

"Based on this study, which will be available at the end of September, we will launch a consultation. But I am repeating that no decision is taken in principle. Perhaps we will not change anything in the current system", he said.
Theodore said the volume in the first six months of 1997 represented 64.3 percent of the total 1996 activity, which amounted to a record 1,417 billion francs.
The daily average during this period rose to 9.09 billion francs, up from a daily average of 5.66 billion francs in 1996.
June was the most active with a total of 245.25 billion francs of funds traded, a record average of 11.68 billion francs per trading day, according to the SBF French bourse association.
The most active session was June 24, with a record 20.01 billion francs transactions (in opening hours only).

Such a strong activity on the secondary market was also seen in the number of transactions registered by the electronic trading system SuperCAC. It rose 38.8 percent from the first half of 1996 with 17.4 million transactions.
The first half was the most active in 11 years for the listing of new companies. A total of 37 French firms were listed, compared with 30 in the first half of 1996.
The amount of funds raised by these new listings rose to 3.15 billion francs from 2.07 billion francs in the first half of 1996, a 52.17 percent progress.
By June 30 French shares' capitalisation was at 3,632 billion francs, up 18.1 percent from 3,073 billion francs by end 1996.
